The logarithms share the same base, so we can combine them using the product rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡(6)+{log}_{5}⁡(2{x}^{2}) & ={log}_{5}⁡(48) \\ {log}_{5}⁡(6\cdot 2{x}^{2}) & ={log}_{5}⁡(48) \\ {log}_{5}⁡(12{x}^{2}) & ={log}_{5}⁡(48)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the equation for $x$ using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{{log}_{5}⁡(12{x}^{2})} & ={5}^{{log}_{5}⁡(48)} \\ 12{x}^{2} & =48 \\ {x}^{2} & =4 \\ x & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x=2$ or $x=-2$

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting them back into the original equation: 

- Substituting $x=2$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡(6)+{log}_{5}⁡(2\cdot {2}^{2}) & \overset{?}{=}{log}_{5}⁡(48) \\ {log}_{5}⁡(6)+{log}_{5}⁡(8) & \overset{?}{=}{log}_{5}⁡(48) \\ {log}_{5}⁡(6\cdot 8) & \overset{?}{=}{log}_{5}⁡(48) \\ {log}_{5}⁡(48) & ={log}_{5}⁡(48).\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=2$ is a valid solution.

- Substituting $x=-2$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡(6)+{log}_{5}⁡(2(-2)^{2}) & \overset{?}{=}{log}_{5}⁡(48) \\ {log}_{5}⁡(6)+{log}_{5}⁡(8) & \overset{?}{=}{log}_{5}⁡(48) \\ {log}_{5}⁡(6\cdot 8) & \overset{?}{=}{log}_{5}⁡(48) \\ {log}_{5}⁡(48) & ={log}_{5}⁡(48).\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=-2$ is a valid solution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$x=\pm 2.$"
